findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: Run now ticks every minute instead of every 10 minutes, so every cleanup job in the slice (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, query history, short URLs, temp files, etc.) runs ten times more often. This is an unrelated global scheduling change not described by the PR and increases database and logging load across the application. Restore the 10-minute interval unless the frequency change is intentional and validated.

findings.title: Normal cleanup progress is logged with Error and full ID lists
findings.body: The cleanup path logs expected normal progress with r.log.Error and includes the entire ids slice. These calls occur for every batch at lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579, so a successful cleanup can emit large error-level log entries containing up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs. Combined with the one-minute cleanup ticker this can flood error logs and add significant I/O. Use debug/info level and avoid dumping full ID lists, and do not include the fetch error in a success-path log message.

findings.title: MaxCount cleanup can delete annotations that should be retained under concurrent deletes
findings.body: The MaxCount cleanup is split into a SELECT that loads excess IDs at OFFSET MaxCount and a later DELETE by those IDs, with no transaction between them. If newer annotations are deleted in that window, rows selected as excess can become part of the newest MaxCount annotations but are still deleted. For example, with MaxCount=1 and annotations id=1 and id=2, cleanup selects id=1 as excess; if a user deletes id=2 before the DELETE runs, cleanup deletes id=1 and leaves zero annotations even though one should have been retained. The PR comment only acknowledges under-deletion from concurrent inserts, not this over-deletion/data-loss case from concurrent deletes.

findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit test does not actually exceed the modern limit
findings.body: The new test creates 40003 annotations but splits them across alert, dashboard and API annotation types, so each per-type cleanup batch fetches at most about 13335 IDs. The configured batch size is 32767, but the actual DELETE statement never contains more than about 13335 IDs. On SQLite >= 3.32.0 the variable limit is 32766, so this test would still pass even if deleteByIDs used placeholders instead of inlining the IDs. It therefore does not exercise the >32767-ID case named by the test; create more than 32767 annotations of a single type or test deleteByIDs directly.
